A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same TSFlow research. All 21 pages of v1 and 23 pages of v2, including figures, tables, equations and appendices, support comparison. Relocated and renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original generation and forecasting experiments on eight datasets, component and conditional-prior-sampling ablations, GPR results and runtime measurements.

after.justification: V2 retains original generation and forecasting experiments and adds guidance, prior, sampling-efficiency, missing-context and multivariate evaluations.

M1.justification: V2 adds a feature-dimension transformer for multivariate forecasting and a seasonal-naive-centered prior variant. It also changes the observed-past conditional prior from Gaussian noise around the observation to a point mass, and revises the guidance noise path and time-dependent guidance scaling. These are substantive procedural and architectural changes.

E1.justification: The eight original datasets remain. V2 adds forecasting with three missing-context scenarios on six datasets and multivariate forecasting on Electricity, Exchange, Solar and Traffic. These expand input conditions and task requirements beyond v1's univariate forecasting with complete context.

E2.justification: The external comparator sets in shared Tables 1–3 remain unchanged. The new missing-context comparisons explicitly use the better conditional or unconditional TSDiff result, expanding beyond v1's unconditional TSDiff framing. V2 also includes a channel-independent TSFlow control in the multivariate comparison.

E3.justification: Reported CPS step size changes from 0.001 to 0.005, noise scale from 0.01 to 0.5, and guidance choices from 4/6 to 8/16/24/32. Conditional-prior preprocessing changes from standardization to mean-centering. New protocols include 50% missingness under three masking patterns, broader NFE sweeps and multivariate CRPS-Sum evaluation. These changes do not establish which earlier experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 adds Gaussian-versus-ALD guidance analysis, a seasonal-naive prior comparison, NFE sensitivity, missing-context robustness tests and a multivariate versus channel-independent comparison. Table 3 also compares four priors within the conditional model. The original component ablation remains, while the standalone GPR-kernel study is removed.

E5.justification: Both versions specify means and standard deviations over five random seeds and show 95% forecast intervals. Additional tables continue the existing reporting practice; revised means and deviations do not establish additional runs or new statistical procedures.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 contain extensive numerical revisions. For example, TSDiff's Wiki2000 Wasserstein distance changes from 183.833 to 214.981, and conditional OU KDDCup CRPS changes from 0.273 to 0.288. V2 adds results for the new analyses and scenarios and removes standalone GPR scores. With method and setting changes, these are revised or newly reported results rather than uniform same-setting gains.

T1.justification: Appendix C replaces linear interpolation of variances with linear interpolation of standard deviations and revises the resulting conditional and marginal vector-field derivation, introducing time-dependent guidance scaling. Equation 4's interpolation sign is corrected from minus to plus. V2 also adds explicit ALD guidance algebra; these changes go beyond equivalent notation.

C1.justification: The central GP-prior flow-matching and conditional/unconditional forecasting contributions remain. V2's abstract replaces the explicit six-of-eight superiority claim with competitive performance, although Section 4.2 retains that claim. The contribution statement shifts from simplifying probability paths to aligning distributions and improving unconditional generation.

C2.justification: V2 adds validation-based kernel selection as a limitation and changes the univariate-only qualification to primarily univariate testing. It explains applicability through observation masks and interprets the guidance-loss comparison. The relocated transport discussion also softens its conclusion from substantially shortening paths to affecting the learning problem.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies noise endpoints in Table 5 and Appendix C, the ALD scale in Appendix A.3, and closed-form ridge regression with 10,000 synthetic samples for LPS in Appendix A.5. It revises sampling and preprocessing instructions. The expanded LPS description documents the existing evaluation rather than establishing a changed procedure.

R1.justification: V2 adds targeted positioning against Tamir et al.'s time-series flow matching and Kerrigan et al.'s functional flow matching. It also adds Luo's tutorial and Park et al.'s prior-based generation work, while removing Chen and Lipman's geometry-related citation. Most related-work framing remains intact.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section sequence remain. Local revisions distinguish flow time from time-series indices, clarify conditioning, update affiliations and publication headers, and reorganize appendix subsections. The transport discussion moves to the appendix and Algorithm 1 moves into the main method section.

P2.justification: V2 redraws the overview and forecast figures, relocates the architecture and transport diagnostic figures to the appendix, and expands Table 3 into separate conditional-prior rows. It adds an NFE figure and six appendix tables while removing the standalone GPR table. This substantially changes the presentation of methods and evidence.

improvement.justification: The added controlled comparisons and missing-context/multivariate tests better support the method's behavior and applicability, and Equation 4 is corrected. These benefits are tempered by unexplained main/appendix score discrepancies, the retained seven-of-eight CPS claim despite Table 8's changed KDDCup result, and new Equation 16 incorrectly equating a score gradient with the loss itself.
